tag: Episode 20 · A Name Is a Debt
title: A Name Is a Debt

beats.t: The spiral stairs rising toward the domed ceiling seemed endless. At every level, rainwater poured between the bookshelves like waterfalls.
Up there! The wet pawprints keep going up.
The stairs are slippery. Stay by the railing.
(Yeongnyangi's cradling his left paw again. He keeps doing it.)
Is your paw okay? You've been walking strangely ever since you fell in the water.
Cats always walk like this. With dignity.
Your dignity is limping.
Then a black current rolled down the stairs from above. Drifting books struck their ankles like fallen leaves.
More water? Does that tiger just turn it on like a faucet?!
The current swallowed three steps at once. Just as Yeoni's feet began lifting off the stairs, warmth stirred around their wrist.
The baby dragon poked out its head and opened wide. The pouring water swirled into its tiny mouth.
You drank more? I told you your belly was going to burst!
The baby dragon answered with a burp. It smelled of rain. Yeoni nearly laughed, then held it in.
It's a storehouse for water. It must not be full yet.
Okay. Unlimited refills today, then.
A dull thud sounded several steps above. A whole section of waterlogged staircase was collapsing.
The stairs are gone. At least five paces to the other side.
(Cats can jump, but I'm a pig. Pigs can't fly five paces.)
Yeoni looked beneath the collapsed stairs. Pale green vines still breathed in the gaps between the wet bookshelves.
Yeongnyangi. Go across first. I'll get there my way.
What way?
Pig-style trapeze.
When Yeoni stretched out a hoof, a vine sprang from a shelf and wound around it. Yeoni threw themself into open air.
The vine bent like a bow, then sprang back. A small pink body cut through the rain and tumbled onto the opposite stairs.
Successful landing! OIIINK! Five stars!
That was a tumble, not a landing.
Tumbling counts as landing. Pig rules.
Yeongnyangi bounded lightly across. As he landed, his left paw buckled for an instant. Yeoni saw, but said nothing.
A small door stood at the stairs' end. Strange light leaked through its cracks. Neither day nor night, but the light of a sun consumed by darkness.
Beyond it was the library roof. A sun hung in the middle of the sky, but half of it had been erased in black.
Is that the sun? Why is half of it missing?
It's been eaten. Remember the black hands appearing on each island? Their master is over there.
At the edge of the roof, the black tiger stood on a rain gutter. Chains dangled from the black book in its mouth, swaying in the wind.
Persistent. Weren't you taught to be quiet in libraries?
I'd rather not hear that from someone who ran off with another person's book.
It isn't someone else's book. It was in my ledger from the start.
Then show me. Your ledger. Why my name is in it.
The tiger did not answer. Instead, it raised a paw. The falling rain gathered at its tips.
All the rainwater on the roof rose at once and crashed toward Yeoni. The baby dragon opened its mouth, but this time there was too much.
Yeoni.
Yeongnyangi leaped in front of them. The torrent struck his navy cloak and pushed the small cat back a step.
Yeongnyangi, move! You can't get hit by water!
That's why I'm telling you to move. Because you can't be hit, either.
In the pause between currents, Yeoni lunged. A vine caught the edge of the tiger's cloak.
The cloak flew wide. The tiger twisted, but Yeoni refused to let go.
And Yeoni saw.
The cloak's lining was densely stitched with gold thread. Amid the gold were several characters sewn in black.
The letters wavered like reflections in water, unreadable. Beside them, a tiny drum-shaped knot and a gray feather were sewn together.
That feather. The one I lost on the crow's island.
And that drum knot. Captain Drum, right? That child's name?
Let go.
Answer, and I will. Why are you keeping his name? You said handing it over to the ledger was the end of it.
Because handing it over is the end. Once it's over, the scars on his wrists will never heal.
Then... you were protecting it?
Don't get the wrong idea. I'm only holding it. I can hand it over any time.
But you haven't yet.
The tiger's red eyes wavered. Rain dripped from its whiskers.
One more question. What's your name?
A name is a debt.
What?
When someone calls it, you owe them. I'm not owing anyone anything ever again.
Then I'll lend to you first. No interest.
I've heard that before. This collar is what it cost.
Something flowed from the sun's black half. Black hands reached out, long as cracks drawn across the sky.
What is taking so long? Bring the book. And the rest of that pig's fortune.
The golden ring at the tiger's neck glowed red-hot. It caught its breath and curled inward.
Hey, your neck. Are you okay?
Move, pig. Stay next to me now, and you'll get swept away, too.
Have you forgotten your debt? What you borrowed from me?
The ring tightened again. Staggering, the tiger dropped the book onto the roof.
The instant the book struck the roof, the chain's padlock split with a sharp crack. The two characters engraved on it sprang up as light.
壬午. Im-o. Yeoni, your Year Pillar.
The light of the two characters flew into Yeoni's chest. The familiar chart appeared before their eyes.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
They're in! Seven. Only one left now!
But Yeoni's smile soon faded. Something was wrong with the first character of the Year Pillar.
[ Year 壬 · Frozen ]
The character 壬 was trapped in black ice. The others glowed warmly, but that one alone did not breathe.
Why is it frozen? I got it, but it feels like I didn't.
Don't try to thaw it.
What?
It will hurt if it melts. You don't need to know what's inside it yet.
The tiger picked up the book in its mouth again. The lock was broken, but black chains still bound the book.
Wait! What's inside? You really were in that spring, weren't you?
The tiger did not look back. Its black body leaped into the rain, becoming rain itself and scattering.
The hands stretching from the sun's black half slowly withdrew, too. As though this was enough for today.
When they returned beneath the domed ceiling, the rain had stopped. Among the soaked books, Moka rolled embers along to dry the shelves.
Back, pig? Judging by your face, it got away again.
It did. But I got something. Halfway.
Halfway? My lady, may I see your chart?
Yeoni held out a hoof. As the chart appeared, Yundal rested his chin on his gloved hand.
壬午. Your Year Pillar. 壬, Im Water, is Direct Resource for you. Water that nurtures and shelters you.
Direct Resource. Like a mother?
Something like that. What Eul Wood born in summer needs most is rain. But that rain is frozen.
What happens when it's frozen?
Still, what has returned has returned. Frozen or not, it's sitting in your place.
So what's the problem with it being frozen? Does it turn into shaved ice?
It doesn't rain. Wood grows thirsty. And when Metal cuts Wood, there's no Water between them to offer support.
Yundal trailed off, glancing at Yeongnyangi. Shaking out and straightening his wet hat, Yeongnyangi looked away as though he hadn't noticed.
Then we just need to melt it.
The one who knows how just turned into rain and disappeared.
Stripes? It froze it and knows how to thaw it? A bigger con artist than you.
I only cheat at compatibility readings. I don't deal in ice.
Admitted to cheating. Everyone heard that, right?
Thank you for remembering me, Mr. Otter. I mean that.
It said it would hurt. If it melted.
Nobody answered. Only Moka's ember gave a little crack.
(The book with my name on it. Captain Drum inside the cloak. A name is a debt. The umbrella someone offered to share.)
(It feels like it all connects, but I can't see the thread yet.)
Yeoni looked up at the chart again. Seven slots were filled. The one remaining blank was the first character of the Hour Pillar.
[ Hour □ · Empty ]
Strange. This slot has been empty since I first met you. There's no trace of theft, unlike the others.
If it wasn't stolen, what is it?
It seems like someone's meant to sit there, but that someone hasn't sat down yet.
Then the empty slot glowed faintly. When Yeoni moved their hoof, the light moved with it. In the direction where it shone brightest stood Yeongnyangi.
Yeongnyangi. It gets brighter toward you.
You're seeing things. Ignore it.
Yeongnyangi stepped back. The glow weakened by that much. Yeoni stepped closer, and it brightened again.
I'm not imagining it.
At that moment, gold flashed deep in Yeongnyangi's eyes. Like sunlight catching a blade.
Yeoni. Let's leave it here for today.
Yeongnyangi turned and walked toward the wet stairs. The sound of his dragging left paw echoed for a long time through the empty library.
